correctness.rationale: The exact beta CDF gives the branching factor. An auxiliary derivative q_b has exactly one turning point and crosses level one once, proving strict unimodality for every b>0; degree two is subcritical and degree three supercritical for b>=4. Scaling x=y/b proves the unique optimum at the root e^y=1+y+y^2. An explicitly uniform fourth-order CDF expansion near k=b^2/2+t b gives the continuous upper root b^2/2-b/6-13/18+O(1/b), with discrete rounding handled separately. Finite exact rational and quadrature checks supplement, not replace, the universal argument. Scope restricted to vulnerable branching under model assumptions.

value.rationale: The theorem provides a complete, natural parameterized susceptibility shape and a sharp distinction between the optimal degree of vulnerable branching (linear in b) and the largest supercritical degree (quadratic in b), including second-order cutoff constants. This gives an analytic benchmark for models of social reinforcement and connectivity, beyond a single-degree computation or known qualitative cascade-window observation. It does not imply predictions of full finite-network diffusion.
